title: Angular Leaf Spot (Cucumber, Melon, Pumpkin, Squash, and Zucchini)
Pseudomonas syringae pv. lachrymans

Prevention: Planting pathogen-free seed is the primary control strategy
Treat contaminated seed with hot water to reduce bacteria levels
Practice a three-year or longer crop rotation to nonhosts such as small grains or corn
Avoid overhead irrigation and reuse of irrigation tail water
Only cultivate and work in fields when the canopy is dry to reduce secondary spread
Plant resistant cucumber varieties if the disease is a recurrent problem
No biological control practices have been developed for angular leaf spot
Monitoring: Look for small, water-soaked lesions on leaves largely confined by large plant veins
Check for angular appearance of lesions (they do not cross plant veins)
Look for clear to milky exudate on the lower surface of lesions during humid weather
Watch for lesions turning tan brown and dropping out of the leaf (shot-hole appearance)
Check fruits for small (0.04 to 0.1 inches) water-soaked lesions with light tan centers
Monitor growing tips in determinate types for systemic infection that stops vine growth
Direct Control: Use Copper-based bactericides (Champ, Kocide, Nordox, Tri Basic Copper) to reduce severity
Apply Champ Dry Prill or Champ Formula 2 at 1.33 lb/pt per acre
Apply Kocide (101, DF, 4.5LF, 3000) at recommended rates (0.5 to 3 lbs/pts)
Apply Nordox at 1.5-2.0 lb per acre
Use Copper/EBDC mixtures like Cuprofix MZ Disperss at 4-7.25 lb
Chemical controls are most effective when integrated with sound cultural control practices
Restrictions: Copper Fungicides: 5-7 days application frequency; may cause plant injury
Copper-Count-N: 7 days application frequency; may cause injury
Cuprofix MZ Disperss: Maximum of 63.1 pounds per season; PHI 5 days
A 4 to 7 day spray interval is necessary when conditions are highly favorable
Always follow product label for specific dosage and timing of application
